# The ledger's engine image, declared once. The yugabyte service runs it, and
# tack-ops receives it as TACK_BACKUP_YB_IMAGE so the backup tooling and the
# restore drill's throwaway engine run the same version the cluster runs. See
# the pin comment on the yugabyte service before changing the tag.
x-yugabyte-image: &yugabyte_image yugabytedb/yugabyte:2024.2.8.0-b85

# The search client environment of the app service. Compose interpolates
# every variable below except OPENSEARCH_CA from the shell environment or
# from the .env file that the configs deploy renders. A shell variable takes
# precedence over the .env file. A variable that neither source sets is
# empty. An empty value selects the compiled default where one exists. An
# empty OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT builds no search runtime and schedules no search
# work. OPENSEARCH_CA is a fixed path. The app reads that CA file from its
# /etc/tack mount. The app service runs the search operator commands, and
# those commands read FoundationDB.
x-opensearch-environment: &opensearch_environment
  OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT: ${OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_CA: /etc/tack/search-ca.crt
  OPENSEARCH_USERNAME: ${OPENSEARCH_USERNAME:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD: ${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD:-}
  OPENSEARCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETRIES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETRIES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PUBLIC_ENABLED: ${OPENSEARCH_PUBLIC_ENABLED:-}
  OPENSEARCH_CURSOR_KEY: ${OPENSEARCH_CURSOR_KEY:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SHARDS: ${OPENSEARCH_SHARDS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_ROUTING_SHARDS: ${OPENSEARCH_ROUTING_SHARDS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_REPLICAS: ${OPENSEARCH_REPLICAS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_TOKEN_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_TOKEN_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BATCHES: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BATCHES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_RESULTS: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_RESULTS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_DEADLINE: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_DEADLINE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PAGE_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_PAGE_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_PAGES: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_PAGES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_SLICE_BUDGET: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_SLICE_BUDGET:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_LEASE: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_LEASE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_IDLE_INTERVAL: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_IDLE_INTERVAL:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_CONCURRENCY: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_CONCURRENCY:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORK_CLASS_WEIGHTS: ${OPENSEARCH_WORK_CLASS_WEIGHTS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIRED_PAGES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIRED_PAGES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIREMENT_AGE: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIREMENT_AGE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_INDEX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_INDEX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_RETENTION_CHECK_INTERVAL: ${OPENSEARCH_RETENTION_CHECK_INTERVAL:-}

services:
  app:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-server:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        COMMIT: ${TACK_COMMIT:-unknown}
        BUILD_TIME: ${TACK_BUILD_TIME:-unknown}
        TAG: ${TACK_TAG:-dev}
        DIRTY: ${TACK_DIRTY:-false}
    # serve is audited like every command: it needs the execute gate and an
    # identity. The app runs as the service identity tack-app, because a
    # long-running daemon is not a human operator (TACK-444).
    command: ["serve", "--execute", "--operator-service", "tack-app"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 1g
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      <<: *opensearch_environment
      # The application's own non-superuser login (TACK-180). tack_app is
      # created by `ops audit seed-roles` from TACK_APP_PASSWORD and holds the
      # three auth tables and nothing else; the yugabyte superuser stays with
      # the ops sidecar for migrations, seeding, and backups.
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://tack_app:${TACK_APP_PASSWORD:?TACK_APP_PASSWORD is required, set it in .env}@yugabyte:5433/${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}?sslmode=disable
      # Audit ledger pools. Each DSN is composed entirely from .env values;
      # if AUDIT_*_PASSWORD is unset the DSN auth fails fast and the audit
      # subsystem degrades to NoopRecorder until seed-audit-roles is run.
      AUDIT_WRITER_DSN: ${AUDIT_WRITER_DSN}
      AUDIT_READER_DSN: ${AUDIT_READER_DSN}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN: ${AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN: ${AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN}
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      # A transaction issued while the store elects a new leader retries
      # without end, bounded only by the caller's context, which not every
      # caller sets. This value bounds it, retries included (TACK-408).
      FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT: ${FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT:-5s}
      PORT: 8000
      # ENV selects the auth mode: development accepts a raw user UUID as the
      # bearer with no token lookup, production requires an API token. It is
      # required rather than defaulted so no environment can start with an
      # auth mode nobody declared; the deploy renders it into .env (TACK-261).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      # Dev policy: noisiest level on, every rotated log kept forever.
      # Logs are append-only history we can grep against post-incident.
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-debug}
      LOG_MAX_BACKUPS: ${LOG_MAX_BACKUPS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS: ${LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB: ${LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB:-100}
      # On-disk paths inside the container. The /var/log/tack volume below
      # binds the host path for cross-restart persistence.
      LOG_JSON_FILE: ${LOG_JSON_FILE:-/var/log/tack/app.jsonl}
      LOG_TEXT_FILE: ${LOG_TEXT_FILE:-/var/log/tack/app.log}
      AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH:-/etc/tack/audit-signing.pem}
      # Valid audit signer set (TACK-437): the key identifiers this environment
      # accepts, rendered per environment by the configs deploy. `audit
      # signers` refuses to run without it; `audit verify` rejects a manifest
      # signed outside it and reports the signer unjudged when it is empty.
      AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS: ${AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS:-}
      # Audit producer. When AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS is set, Record publishes to
      # Kafka and the audit-consumer becomes the only writer of audit.events.
      # Empty uses the synchronous Yugabyte recorder.
      AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS:-}
      AUDIT_KAFKA_TOPIC: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_TOPIC:-audit.events.v1}
      AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID:-tack-audit-producer}
      # Matches the application default. A hard broker loss costs up to 9s of
      # broker lease expiry plus up to 5s of client metadata refresh, so a
      # smaller budget expires while delivery would still have succeeded.
      AUDIT_KAFKA_PRODUCE_TIMEOUT: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_PRODUCE_TIMEOUT:-15s}
      # QA data generator write marker, read only by `ops qa datagen`. The
      # generator refuses to write unless this is exactly qa or local, so the
      # value is set on tack-qa and left empty on production. The app service
      # carries it because the generator needs FoundationDB reachability and the
      # audit DSNs, which the host-networked tack-ops container does not have.
      TACK_DATAGEN_ALLOW_TARGET: ${TACK_DATAGEN_ALLOW_TARGET:-}
      # Backup object store. Empty unless the host's group_vars set them; read only by ops backup.
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION:-us-east-1}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN:-tack-backups}
    volumes:
      # Writable, because the FoundationDB client writes the new coordinator
      # list into this file when the cluster changes coordinators. Mounted
      # read-only, the client keeps the coordinators it started with and stops
      # finding the cluster once every one of them is gone (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      - tack-logs:/var/log/tack
      # Audit ledger signing key. Generated once on the host with
      #   openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out /etc/tack/audit-signing.pem
      # The notarizer reuses it at every 60s tick; rotation is a follow-up.
      - /etc/tack:/etc/tack:ro
    # No yugabyte dependency: deployed guests reach the ledger on the data
    # guests through the rendered override's multi-host URL, and the deploy
    # starts the app only after provision. This base file alone still dials
    # the local single node above and relies on restart for ordering.
    #
    # No fdb dependency either. Deployed guests reach the product store on the
    # data guests through the coordinator list in the cluster file, and the
    # owner guest runs no store process after phase 4, so a dependency here
    # would start one (TACK-408). Locally the app restarts until the store
    # answers, the same ordering the ledger relies on.

  yugabyte:
    # Pinned to 2024.2.8.0-b85 to match the running production engine. The audit
    # Kafka cutover must change only the audit pipeline, not the database engine:
    # a deploy that bumped this image would perform an untested in-place
    # major-version upgrade of the auth+audit database (TACK-330). The deliberate
    # 2024.2.8.0 -> 2025.2.3.0 upgrade is the separate, QA-validated TACK-329.
    #
    # Identity is a permanent name, never an address. The engine writes the
    # announced identity into its own catalog, so an address written there goes
    # stale when the address moves and the engine can no longer assemble itself
    # to serve rows that are intact on disk. Replaceable container addresses
    # persisted into that catalog caused an incident.
    #
    # The deploy renders a docker-compose.override.yml beside this file;
    # compose merges it automatically. The override replaces hostname with
    # the guest's node name, adds extra_hosts mapping the peer names to the
    # peer guests' pinned addresses (reached on the published node ports),
    # and replaces this whole command list, because compose only replaces a
    # command wholesale: the replacement changes only the advertise and
    # listen name and must keep the flagfile argument verbatim, or the
    # tserver silently reverts to self-sizing (the 2026-08-05 S0). A node
    # binds exactly what it announces, because yugabyted refuses to start
    # when the two differ, so a node's own name must resolve inside its own
    # container to an address it can bind; hostname is what maps it there.
    #
    # The :ro bind-mount below patches yugabyted's is_port_available. The
    # upstream version (on every release through 2025.2.3.0, including this one)
    # builds an AF_INET socket for any non-literal-v6 advertise_address, which
    # raises gaierror on this v6-only bridge before yugabyted ever binds.
    # Upstream PR #23158 fixes it with AF_UNSPEC getaddrinfo + iterate; it has
    # been open since 2024-07 with no movement. We apply the same patch via
    # the overlay in yugabyte-overlay/yugabyted until upstream lands a fix.
    # See AGENTS.md "YugabyteDB identity and data contract" for the full story
    # and the refresh procedure on image bump. The tag itself is the
    # x-yugabyte-image anchor at the top of this file.
    image: *yugabyte_image
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 10g
    # The container answers to the name this node announces, which is what maps
    # that name to this container's own address. This is the dev value; the
    # deploy's rendered override replaces it with the guest's node name.
    hostname: yugabyte
    # --base_dir aims yugabyted at the persisted volume mount below. Without
    # it, yugabyted defaults to ~/var, which is the container overlay and is
    # lost on every recreate: a docker compose down then wipes the SQL side
    # (2026-04-28 incident).
    # The tserver resource bounds live in yugabyte-overlay/tserver.flags,
    # mounted below; flagfile hands them to the tserver one flag per line.
    command:
      - /home/yugabyte/bin/yugabyted
      - start
      - --daemon=false
      - --base_dir=/home/yugabyte/var
      - --advertise_address=yugabyte
      - --listen=yugabyte
      - --tserver_flags=flagfile=/home/yugabyte/tserver.flags
    environment:
      YSQL_DB: ${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}
      # yugabyted reads the superuser name and password only on the first
      # start of an empty data directory. The deploy passes them for that
      # start from the vault and renders neither into .env (TACK-554). A
      # first start with an empty password creates the superuser with the
      # engine's default password. On that first start the health check
      # below logs in with the password, which yugabyted sets after the
      # database accepts connections.
      YSQL_USER: ${YUGABYTE_USER:-}
      YSQL_PASSWORD: ${YUGABYTE_PASSWORD:-}
    ports:
      - "5433:5433" # YSQL (Postgres-compatible)
      - "7000:7000" # YugabyteDB master UI
      - "9000:9000" # YugabyteDB tserver UI
      # Peer nodes reach this one on the guest's pinned address at these ports.
      - "7100:7100" # master peer traffic
      - "9100:9100" # tserver peer traffic
    volumes:
      - yugabyte-data:/home/yugabyte/var
      # Overlay patched yugabyted (upstream PR #23158). See header comment.
      - /root/tack/yugabyte-overlay/yugabyted:/home/yugabyte/bin/yugabyted:ro
      # Tserver resource bounds, one flag per line with the incident notes.
      - /root/tack/yugabyte-overlay/tserver.flags:/home/yugabyte/tserver.flags:ro
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - |
          if [ -n "$$YSQL_PASSWORD" ]; then
            PGPASSWORD="$$YSQL_PASSWORD" ysqlsh -h "$$(hostname)" -p 5433 \
              -U "$$YSQL_USER" -d "$$YSQL_DB" -c 'SELECT 1' -t
          else
            /home/yugabyte/postgres/bin/pg_isready -h "$$(hostname)" -p 5433
          fi
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      # This status is informational: the deploy's rolling wait is keyed on
      # the node's tablet bootstrap progress, not on this check (TACK-488).
      # The engine has no graceful stop, so every restart replays each
      # tablet's open log segments before the SQL layer answers; the start
      # period covers a small node's replay so its status does not flap to
      # unhealthy on an ordinary restart. A full node takes longer and shows
      # unhealthy until its replay ends, then healthy again on the next
      # passing check.
      start_period: 180s

  fdb:
    # Version is set by tack's Makefile FDB_VERSION variable, also baked
    # into the Dockerfile build args and the Go bindings pin in go.mod.
    # Bump all three together via make update-fdb VERSION=...
    image: foundationdb/foundationdb:${FDB_VERSION:-7.4.6}
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      FDB_NETWORKING_MODE: container
      FDB_PORT: "4500"
      FDB_PROCESS_CLASS: unset
      # One cluster file for the server process and for every client on this
      # guest. The image defaults the server to /var/fdb/fdb.cluster, a second
      # file the clients never read, so a coordinator change the server wrote
      # there reached nobody (TACK-408).
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      # This guest's identity in the cluster, rendered by the deploy from the
      # service inventory. The address is the guest's pinned address, which
      # peers and clients on other guests reach and which survives a container
      # recreate; the zone is the guest name, which is the fault domain the
      # replication counts. Empty here so a local `docker compose up` keeps
      # announcing the container's own address and hostname.
      FDB_PUBLIC_ADDRESS: ${FDB_PUBLIC_ADDRESS:-}
      FDB_ZONE_ID: ${FDB_ZONE_ID:-}
      FDB_MACHINE_ID: ${FDB_MACHINE_ID:-}
      # The coordinator list a guest's first process starts from. The deploy
      # renders the environment's three coordinators; a guest that already has
      # a cluster file ignores this, because the cluster owns that file once it
      # exists. Empty locally, where the process is its own coordinator.
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE_CONTENTS: ${FDB_CLUSTER_FILE_CONTENTS:-}
    volumes:
      - fdb-data:/var/fdb
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      # Patched fdb.bash with IPv6 bracket handling. See fdb-overlay/fdb.bash.
      - /root/tack/fdb-overlay/fdb.bash:/var/fdb/scripts/fdb.bash:ro
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "fdbcli -C /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster --exec 'status minimal' 2>&1 | grep -q 'available'",
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # Long-lived backup_agent that streams FoundationDB continuous backups to the
  # object store. The fdbbackup session is started by `ops provision` on a host
  # whose TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS is true, and by `ops backup
  # fdb-continuous-init` for a deliberate out-of-band start; both are idempotent,
  # so an already-streaming session is left alone. This agent drains the
  # session's snapshots. The backup
  # profile keeps it off for a plain `docker compose up` without an object store,
  # and the deploy enables the profile. fdbbackup cannot resolve an IPv6 literal,
  # so it reaches the blobstore through the synthetic name fdb-blobstore-host
  # mapped to TACK_BACKUP_S3_HOST, the bare object-store address configs renders
  # alongside the full TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT.
  #
  # One agent runs per data guest. Agents divide the session's work between
  # themselves, so the count is a throughput and survival choice rather than a
  # configuration the session records: the session keeps streaming while any
  # one agent runs (TACK-408). It declares no fdb dependency, because the agent
  # retries its own connection and because a dependency would start the store
  # process on the owner guest, which runs none.
  fdb-backup-agent:
    image: foundationdb/foundationdb:${FDB_VERSION:-7.4.6}
    profiles: [backup]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 512m
    entrypoint: ["/usr/bin/backup_agent"]
    command: ["-C", "/etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster"]
    extra_hosts:
      - "fdb-blobstore-host:${TACK_BACKUP_S3_HOST}"
    volumes:
      # Writable for the same reason the app's mount is: the agent is a
      # FoundationDB client, and its client library records a coordinator
      # change in this file.
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb

  # OpenSearch, one member per search guest. Every member takes the
  # cluster_manager, data, ingest, and ml roles, and a later member joins the
  # running cluster with no Tack change. Compose starts this service only
  # when the search profile is enabled. The deploy enables the search profile
  # on the search guests and on no other guest.
  #
  # Compose interpolates node.name and the three discovery settings from the
  # TACK_SEARCH_* values in the shell environment or the rendered .env file.
  # A shell variable takes precedence over the .env file. The other values in this
  # service are literals, and the rendered override on a search guest can
  # replace them. QA sets TACK_SEARCH_DISCOVERY_TYPE to single-node.
  # Production sets TACK_SEARCH_SEED_HOSTS from the member list, and sets
  # TACK_SEARCH_INITIAL_CLUSTER_MANAGER_NODES only for the first formation of
  # tack-search1. The image entrypoint passes each non-empty dotted variable as
  # a setting, and an empty one leaves that setting unset. The rendered
  # override also configures TLS, credentials, and the address a member
  # announces to its peers.
  #
  # The search guests have no IPv4 route. java.net.preferIPv6Addresses makes
  # the JVM connect to the IPv6 address of a dual-stack host, such as the
  # model artifact host that ML Commons downloads the pinned model from.
  #
  # The ML Commons memory breaker rejects predictions when used heap is at or
  # above 85 percent. G1PeriodicGCInterval=5000 enables periodic garbage
  # collection.
  opensearch:
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch:3.8.0
    profiles: [search]
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS: -Xms3g -Xmx3g -XX:G1PeriodicGCInterval=5000 -Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true
      node.roles: cluster_manager,data,ingest,ml
      node.name: ${TACK_SEARCH_NODE_NAME:-}
      discovery.type: ${TACK_SEARCH_DISCOVERY_TYPE:-}
      discovery.seed_hosts: ${TACK_SEARCH_SEED_HOSTS:-}
      cluster.initial_cluster_manager_nodes: ${TACK_SEARCH_INITIAL_CLUSTER_MANAGER_NODES:-}
    volumes:
      - opensearch-data:/usr/share/opensearch/data
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536

  # Apache Kafka 4.x in KRaft combined broker+controller role. The audit
  # cutover uses this as the broker for the audit.events.v1 topic that the
  # producer publishes to and the audit-consumer projects into audit.events.
  #
  # The cluster ID is pinned to a value generated once on the host with:
  #
  #   docker run --rm apache/kafka:4.2.0 \
  #     /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-storage.sh random-uuid
  #
  # Persist the result into KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID in .env so a recreate does
  # not stamp a fresh metadata directory and orphan the existing logs.
  # No external port is exposed: traffic stays inside the IPv6 bridge.
  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:4.2.0
    profiles: [audit]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "1"
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:9093
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://[::]:9092,CONTROLLER://[::]:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: "1"
      KAFKA_NUM_PARTITIONS: "256"
      KAFKA_DEFAULT_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_MIN_INSYNC_REPLICAS: "1"
      KAFKA_UNCLEAN_LEADER_ELECTION_ENABLE: "false"
      # Empty default so the core stack parses while kafka is profile-gated off.
      # The audit-profile deploy must set KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID (a kafka-storage.sh
      # random-uuid) in .env before enabling the audit profile.
      CLUSTER_ID: ${KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID:-}
    volumes:
      - kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 >/dev/null 2>&1
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # ClickHouse single-node OLAP store for the Wave 1 audit consumer.
  # Internal-only: 8123 (HTTP) and 9000 (native) are not exposed to the
  # host. Apache 2.0 image so the open-source-only constraint holds.
  clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.5
    profiles: [audit]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DEFAULT_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: "1"
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O - http://[::1]:8123/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # Wave 1 audit-consumer. Uses the same image as the app container; the
  # entrypoint is overridden to /usr/local/bin/audit-consumer so the
  # binary built by the Dockerfile is invoked directly. Mounts the
  # signing key for the embedded notarizer.
  audit-consumer:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-audit-consumer:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [audit]
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.audit-consumer
      args:
        COMMIT: ${TACK_COMMIT:-unknown}
        BUILD_TIME: ${TACK_BUILD_TIME:-unknown}
        TAG: ${TACK_TAG:-dev}
        DIRTY: ${TACK_DIRTY:-false}
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 1g
    entrypoint: ["/usr/local/bin/audit-consumer"]
    environment:
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_BROKERS: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_BROKERS:-kafka:9092}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_TOPIC: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_TOPIC:-audit.events.v1}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID:-tack-audit-projector}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_BATCH_SIZE: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_BATCH_SIZE:-256}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_POLL_INTERVAL: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_POLL_INTERVAL:-250ms}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_YUGABYTE_DSN: ${AUDIT_WRITER_DSN}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_CLICKHOUSE_DSN: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_CLICKHOUSE_DSN:-clickhouse://default:@clickhouse:9000/audit}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_KEY_PATH:-/etc/tack/audit-signing.pem}
      # The guest whose key signs, stamped on every notarization as its
      # claimed origin (TACK-437). The configs deploy renders the guest's
      # inventory name; empty falls back to the container's hostname.
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_HOST: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_HOST:-}
      # Set this to enable the FoundationDB half of the operator relay. It is
      # deliberately not hardcoded: a set-but-unreadable cluster file makes the
      # consumer refuse to start, which would also stop the YugabyteDB relay
      # and halt every operator event, not just the FoundationDB ones. Leaving
      # it unset on a host without that mount runs the YugabyteDB half alone.
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_FDB_CLUSTER_FILE:-}
      # The same ENV the app requires, read the same way, so every consumer
      # log line names its environment (TACK-263).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-debug}
      LOG_JSON_FILE: /var/log/tack/audit-consumer.jsonl
      LOG_TEXT_FILE: /var/log/tack/audit-consumer.log
      LOG_MAX_BACKUPS: ${LOG_MAX_BACKUPS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS: ${LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB: ${LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB:-100}
    volumes:
      - tack-logs:/var/log/tack
      - /etc/tack:/etc/tack:ro
      # Writable: this process is a FoundationDB client too, and the client
      # library records a coordinator change in this file (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
    # No yugabyte dependency: deployed guests reach the ledger on the data
    # guests through the rendered env's multi-host DSN; the startup ping
    # retries until the ledger answers, so ordering is not load-bearing.
    depends_on:
      kafka:
        condition: service_started
      clickhouse:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Short-lived operator-invoked container for backup, verify, and
  # restore-test operations. The profiles: [ops] tag keeps it out of the
  # default docker compose up; invoke via:
  #   docker compose run --rm tack-ops ops backup [subcommand] [args]
  tack-ops:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-server:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [ops]
    mem_limit: 512m
    entrypoint: ["/server"]
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      # tack-ops uses network_mode: host so all services are reachable by
      # loopback. DATABASE_URL must be set in the host .env as a full DSN
      # pointing at 127.0.0.1:5433; the app service's DSN targets yugabyte
      # and cannot be reused here.
      DATABASE_URL: ${TACK_OPS_DATABASE_URL}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN:-}
      # Ledger read and redaction for the `audit query`, `audit get`,
      # `audit export`, and `audit redact-actor` host commands. Loopback DSNs
      # like the operator one above; empty until the host .env renders them.
      AUDIT_READER_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_READER_DSN:-}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN:-}
      # The valid signer set (TACK-437), the same value the app carries, so
      # `audit verify` here judges a bundle's signer. `audit signers` still
      # runs through the app service: this container mounts no signing key.
      AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS: ${AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS:-}
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT: ${FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT:-5s}
      # The redundancy mode `ops provision` configures on a store that has
      # never been configured. single is the local and single-guest value;
      # an environment running one process per data guest renders double, so
      # a rebuilt environment comes back with the replication it had rather
      # than with one copy of every key (TACK-408).
      TACK_OPS_FDB_REDUNDANCY_MODE: ${TACK_OPS_FDB_REDUNDANCY_MODE:-single}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      # Same ENV the app requires, read the same way. A default here would
      # make one variable name mean two things in one stack file, so a host
      # whose .env said development would still run this container as
      # production (TACK-261).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      # The database that the backup dumps read. The dumps connect as
      # tack_migrator with TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD below.
      YUGABYTE_DB: ${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}
      # Audit role passwords for `ops audit seed-roles`, which creates or rotates
      # the LOGIN audit roles. Empty default so other ops (backup) run without
      # them; the seed-roles command errors loudly when they are unset.
      AUDIT_WRITER_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_WRITER_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_READER_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_READER_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_REDACTOR_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_OPERATOR_PASSWORD:-}
      # The application login's password, set by the same seed-roles run
      # (TACK-180); the app service reads it inside its DATABASE_URL.
      TACK_APP_PASSWORD: ${TACK_APP_PASSWORD:-}
      TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD: ${TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD:-}
      # Object store for engine-native continuous backup. Read by the FDB
      # continuous backup path to build the blobstore destination URL.
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION:-us-east-1}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN:-tack-backups}
      # Master quorum for the backup one-shot containers. The deploy renders
      # the value from the ledger topology; the fallback is the dev single
      # node, matching the compiled default.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_MASTER_ADDRESSES: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_MASTER_ADDRESSES:-yugabyte:7100}
      # Ledger node names paired with their guests' addresses (TACK-460), so
      # the SQL dumpers can dial an encrypted node by the name its
      # certificate carries. The deploy renders it; empty in the clear.
      TACK_LEDGER_NODE_HOSTS: ${TACK_LEDGER_NODE_HOSTS:-}
      # The ledger's own image, from the anchor the yugabyte service uses. The
      # backup tooling (yb-admin, ysql_dump, ysql_dumpall) and the restore
      # drill's throwaway engine run it, so a rehearsal restores into the
      # version the cluster runs and the dumper matches the server. There is
      # no compiled default: a default in the binary drifted to 2025.2 against
      # this 2024.2 cluster, and the drill's schema apply failed on it.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_IMAGE: *yugabyte_image
      # Snapshot-export paths. Deliberately no fallback: the commands that
      # need them error loudly when unset, per the config contract, rather
      # than tar or restore against a wrong location.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_ROCKSDB_DIR: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_ROCKSDB_DIR:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_OVERLAY_PATH: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_OVERLAY_PATH:-}
      # Backup staleness alarm mail. A staleness-check run that first finds a
      # mechanism past its threshold mails a plain-words account of the fault.
      # Empty recipient mails nothing, which is the local default; the deploy
      # renders the address.
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_EMAIL: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_EMAIL:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_MSMTPRC: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_MSMTPRC:-/etc/msmtprc}
      # Deputy staleness alarm (TACK-481): the primary checker's service name,
      # the window its run must appear in, and the in-run grace before the
      # deputy takes over. An empty service means this checker is the primary.
      # Without this pass-through a data guest's check ran as a primary and
      # mailed a second time for the same fault.
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_SERVICE: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_SERVICE:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_WINDOW_SECONDS: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_WINDOW_SECONDS:-1500}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_GRACE_SECONDS: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_GRACE_SECONDS:-90}
      # FoundationDB continuous backup. Without this pass-through the container
      # falls back to the compiled default false, so `ops provision` leaves the
      # stream off and the restore drill and staleness check skip their FDB legs
      # on a host whose .env says true. The overlay path is the patched fdb.bash
      # the deploy places on the guest, which the restore drill bind-mounts into
      # its throwaway cluster; deliberately no fallback, so the drill errors
      # loudly when it is unset rather than mounting a wrong file.
      TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS: ${TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS:-false}
      TACK_BACKUP_FDB_OVERLAY_PATH: ${TACK_BACKUP_FDB_OVERLAY_PATH:-}
      # Ledger transport encryption (TACK-460). The ledger DSNs above already
      # carry sslmode and the authority's path; these two are for the engine's
      # administration tool, which the backup and snapshot commands run in
      # one-shot containers and which takes its certificate directory as a
      # flag. Without the pass-through those commands dial an encrypted
      # cluster with no certificates and fail to connect.
      TACK_LEDGER_TLS_ENABLED: ${TACK_LEDGER_TLS_ENABLED:-false}
      TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR: ${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-}
      # The tag this stack pins the app images at, so `ops deploy verify`
      # checks the running containers against the image the deploy named.
      TACK_IMAGE_TAG: ${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    volumes:
      - /root/backups:/root/backups
      # Writable: the ops commands that open the product store are
      # FoundationDB clients, and the client library records a coordinator
      # change in this file (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      # The staleness alarm reads the guest's SMTP account out of this file and
      # then speaks SMTP itself, so the file is all it needs: no msmtp binary
      # lives in this image, and nothing here execs one.
      - /etc/msmtprc:/etc/msmtprc:ro
      # The ledger's certificate authority, for the DSNs above and for the
      # one-shots this container starts. Only the certificate directory, not
      # the whole of /etc/tack: the audit signing key lives beside it and this
      # container deliberately holds no signing key.
      - ${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-/etc/tack/ledger-certs}:${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-/etc/tack/ledger-certs}:ro
      # Docker socket mount is intentional for this short-lived ops container:
      # the backup binary orchestrates scratch containers on the local daemon.
      # This exception is explicitly scoped to tack-ops and must not be added
      # to the long-running app service. See the sibling-container architecture
      # decision in CLAUDE.md under the Deployment section.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

volumes:
  yugabyte-data:
  fdb-data:
  tack-logs:
  kafka-data:
  clickhouse-data:
  opensearch-data:

# IPv6-only bridge. The per-host /96 is carved from the host's on-link /64 and
# NDP-proxied back onto eth0 by ndppd, so containers source out as real GUAs
# (gateway_mode_v6 is routed, no masquerade). Inter-container DNS returns AAAA
# only because enable_ipv4 is false. Do not flip back to dual-stack: that defeats
# the forced-v6 contract. The subnet and gateway are per host and come from the
# configs render (tack_docker_v6_subnet / tack_docker_v6_gateway); the defaults
# are the production prefix so an unrendered env still parses.
networks:
  default:
    enable_ipv6: true
    enable_ipv4: false
    driver_opts:
      com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_v6: routed
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${TACK_DOCKER_V6_SUBNET:-3d06:bad:b01:0:7ac::/96}
          gateway: ${TACK_DOCKER_V6_GATEWAY:-3d06:bad:b01:0:7ac::1}

files.current_content:
# The ledger's engine image, declared once. The yugabyte service runs it, and
# tack-ops receives it as TACK_BACKUP_YB_IMAGE so the backup tooling and the
# restore drill's throwaway engine run the same version the cluster runs. See
# the pin comment on the yugabyte service before changing the tag.
x-yugabyte-image: &yugabyte_image yugabytedb/yugabyte:2024.2.8.0-b85

# The search client environment of the app service. Compose interpolates
# every variable below except OPENSEARCH_CA from the shell environment or
# from the .env file that the configs deploy renders. A shell variable takes
# precedence over the .env file. A variable that neither source sets is
# empty. An empty value selects the compiled default where one exists. An
# empty OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT builds no search runtime and schedules no search
# work. OPENSEARCH_CA is a fixed path. The app reads that CA file from its
# /etc/tack mount. The app service runs the search operator commands, and
# those commands read FoundationDB.
x-opensearch-environment: &opensearch_environment
  OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT: ${OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_CA: /etc/tack/search-ca.crt
  OPENSEARCH_USERNAME: ${OPENSEARCH_USERNAME:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD: ${OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD:-}
  OPENSEARCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETRIES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETRIES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PUBLIC_ENABLED: ${OPENSEARCH_PUBLIC_ENABLED:-}
  OPENSEARCH_CURSOR_KEY: ${OPENSEARCH_CURSOR_KEY:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SHARDS: ${OPENSEARCH_SHARDS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_ROUTING_SHARDS: ${OPENSEARCH_ROUTING_SHARDS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_REPLICAS: ${OPENSEARCH_REPLICAS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_TOKEN_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_TOKEN_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BATCHES: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BATCHES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_RESULTS: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_MAX_RESULTS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_QUERY_DEADLINE: ${OPENSEARCH_QUERY_DEADLINE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_PAGE_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_PAGE_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_PAGES: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_PAGES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_MAX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_SLICE_BUDGET: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_SLICE_BUDGET:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_LEASE: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_LEASE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_IDLE_INTERVAL: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_IDLE_INTERVAL:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORKER_CONCURRENCY: ${OPENSEARCH_WORKER_CONCURRENCY:-}
  OPENSEARCH_WORK_CLASS_WEIGHTS: ${OPENSEARCH_WORK_CLASS_WEIGHTS:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIRED_PAGES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIRED_PAGES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIREMENT_AGE: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_RETIREMENT_AGE:-}
  OPENSEARCH_MAX_INDEX_BYTES: ${OPENSEARCH_MAX_INDEX_BYTES:-}
  OPENSEARCH_RETENTION_CHECK_INTERVAL: ${OPENSEARCH_RETENTION_CHECK_INTERVAL:-}

services:
  app:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-server:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        COMMIT: ${TACK_COMMIT:-unknown}
        BUILD_TIME: ${TACK_BUILD_TIME:-unknown}
        TAG: ${TACK_TAG:-dev}
        DIRTY: ${TACK_DIRTY:-false}
    # serve is audited like every command: it needs the execute gate and an
    # identity. The app runs as the service identity tack-app, because a
    # long-running daemon is not a human operator (TACK-444).
    command: ["serve", "--execute", "--operator-service", "tack-app"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 1g
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      <<: *opensearch_environment
      # The application's own non-superuser login (TACK-180). tack_app is
      # created by `ops audit seed-roles` from TACK_APP_PASSWORD and holds the
      # three auth tables and nothing else; the yugabyte superuser stays with
      # the ops sidecar for migrations, seeding, and backups.
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://tack_app:${TACK_APP_PASSWORD:?TACK_APP_PASSWORD is required, set it in .env}@yugabyte:5433/${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}?sslmode=disable
      # Audit ledger pools. Each DSN is composed entirely from .env values;
      # if AUDIT_*_PASSWORD is unset the DSN auth fails fast and the audit
      # subsystem degrades to NoopRecorder until seed-audit-roles is run.
      AUDIT_WRITER_DSN: ${AUDIT_WRITER_DSN}
      AUDIT_READER_DSN: ${AUDIT_READER_DSN}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN: ${AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN: ${AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN}
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      # A transaction issued while the store elects a new leader retries
      # without end, bounded only by the caller's context, which not every
      # caller sets. This value bounds it, retries included (TACK-408).
      FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT: ${FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT:-5s}
      PORT: 8000
      # ENV selects the auth mode: development accepts a raw user UUID as the
      # bearer with no token lookup, production requires an API token. It is
      # required rather than defaulted so no environment can start with an
      # auth mode nobody declared; the deploy renders it into .env (TACK-261).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      # Dev policy: noisiest level on, every rotated log kept forever.
      # Logs are append-only history we can grep against post-incident.
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-debug}
      LOG_MAX_BACKUPS: ${LOG_MAX_BACKUPS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS: ${LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB: ${LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB:-100}
      # On-disk paths inside the container. The /var/log/tack volume below
      # binds the host path for cross-restart persistence.
      LOG_JSON_FILE: ${LOG_JSON_FILE:-/var/log/tack/app.jsonl}
      LOG_TEXT_FILE: ${LOG_TEXT_FILE:-/var/log/tack/app.log}
      AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY_PATH:-/etc/tack/audit-signing.pem}
      # Valid audit signer set (TACK-437): the key identifiers this environment
      # accepts, rendered per environment by the configs deploy. `audit
      # signers` refuses to run without it; `audit verify` rejects a manifest
      # signed outside it and reports the signer unjudged when it is empty.
      AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS: ${AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS:-}
      # Audit producer. When AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS is set, Record publishes to
      # Kafka and the audit-consumer becomes the only writer of audit.events.
      # Empty uses the synchronous Yugabyte recorder.
      AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS:-}
      AUDIT_KAFKA_TOPIC: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_TOPIC:-audit.events.v1}
      AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID:-tack-audit-producer}
      # Matches the application default. A hard broker loss costs up to 9s of
      # broker lease expiry plus up to 5s of client metadata refresh, so a
      # smaller budget expires while delivery would still have succeeded.
      AUDIT_KAFKA_PRODUCE_TIMEOUT: ${AUDIT_KAFKA_PRODUCE_TIMEOUT:-15s}
      # QA data generator write marker, read only by `ops qa datagen`. The
      # generator refuses to write unless this is exactly qa or local, so the
      # value is set on tack-qa and left empty on production. The app service
      # carries it because the generator needs FoundationDB reachability and the
      # audit DSNs, which the host-networked tack-ops container does not have.
      TACK_DATAGEN_ALLOW_TARGET: ${TACK_DATAGEN_ALLOW_TARGET:-}
      # Backup object store. Empty unless the host's group_vars set them; read only by ops backup.
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION:-us-east-1}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN:-tack-backups}
    volumes:
      # Writable, because the FoundationDB client writes the new coordinator
      # list into this file when the cluster changes coordinators. Mounted
      # read-only, the client keeps the coordinators it started with and stops
      # finding the cluster once every one of them is gone (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      - tack-logs:/var/log/tack
      # Audit ledger signing key. Generated once on the host with
      #   openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out /etc/tack/audit-signing.pem
      # The notarizer reuses it at every 60s tick; rotation is a follow-up.
      - /etc/tack:/etc/tack:ro
    # No yugabyte dependency: deployed guests reach the ledger on the data
    # guests through the rendered override's multi-host URL, and the deploy
    # starts the app only after provision. This base file alone still dials
    # the local single node above and relies on restart for ordering.
    #
    # No fdb dependency either. Deployed guests reach the product store on the
    # data guests through the coordinator list in the cluster file, and the
    # owner guest runs no store process after phase 4, so a dependency here
    # would start one (TACK-408). Locally the app restarts until the store
    # answers, the same ordering the ledger relies on.

  yugabyte:
    # Pinned to 2024.2.8.0-b85 to match the running production engine. The audit
    # Kafka cutover must change only the audit pipeline, not the database engine:
    # a deploy that bumped this image would perform an untested in-place
    # major-version upgrade of the auth+audit database (TACK-330). The deliberate
    # 2024.2.8.0 -> 2025.2.3.0 upgrade is the separate, QA-validated TACK-329.
    #
    # Identity is a permanent name, never an address. The engine writes the
    # announced identity into its own catalog, so an address written there goes
    # stale when the address moves and the engine can no longer assemble itself
    # to serve rows that are intact on disk. Replaceable container addresses
    # persisted into that catalog caused an incident.
    #
    # The deploy renders a docker-compose.override.yml beside this file;
    # compose merges it automatically. The override replaces hostname with
    # the guest's node name, adds extra_hosts mapping the peer names to the
    # peer guests' pinned addresses (reached on the published node ports),
    # and replaces this whole command list, because compose only replaces a
    # command wholesale: the replacement changes only the advertise and
    # listen name and must keep the flagfile argument verbatim, or the
    # tserver silently reverts to self-sizing (the 2026-08-05 S0). A node
    # binds exactly what it announces, because yugabyted refuses to start
    # when the two differ, so a node's own name must resolve inside its own
    # container to an address it can bind; hostname is what maps it there.
    #
    # The :ro bind-mount below patches yugabyted's is_port_available. The
    # upstream version (on every release through 2025.2.3.0, including this one)
    # builds an AF_INET socket for any non-literal-v6 advertise_address, which
    # raises gaierror on this v6-only bridge before yugabyted ever binds.
    # Upstream PR #23158 fixes it with AF_UNSPEC getaddrinfo + iterate; it has
    # been open since 2024-07 with no movement. We apply the same patch via
    # the overlay in yugabyte-overlay/yugabyted until upstream lands a fix.
    # See AGENTS.md "YugabyteDB identity and data contract" for the full story
    # and the refresh procedure on image bump. The tag itself is the
    # x-yugabyte-image anchor at the top of this file.
    image: *yugabyte_image
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 10g
    # The container answers to the name this node announces, which is what maps
    # that name to this container's own address. This is the dev value; the
    # deploy's rendered override replaces it with the guest's node name.
    hostname: yugabyte
    # --base_dir aims yugabyted at the persisted volume mount below. Without
    # it, yugabyted defaults to ~/var, which is the container overlay and is
    # lost on every recreate: a docker compose down then wipes the SQL side
    # (2026-04-28 incident).
    # The tserver resource bounds live in yugabyte-overlay/tserver.flags,
    # mounted below; flagfile hands them to the tserver one flag per line.
    command:
      - /home/yugabyte/bin/yugabyted
      - start
      - --daemon=false
      - --base_dir=/home/yugabyte/var
      - --advertise_address=yugabyte
      - --listen=yugabyte
      - --tserver_flags=flagfile=/home/yugabyte/tserver.flags
    environment:
      YSQL_DB: ${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}
      # yugabyted reads the superuser name and password only on the first
      # start of an empty data directory. The deploy passes them for that
      # start from the vault and renders neither into .env (TACK-554). A
      # first start with an empty password creates the superuser with the
      # engine's default password. On that first start the health check
      # below logs in with the password, which yugabyted sets after the
      # database accepts connections.
      YSQL_USER: ${YUGABYTE_USER:-}
      YSQL_PASSWORD: ${YUGABYTE_PASSWORD:-}
    ports:
      - "5433:5433" # YSQL (Postgres-compatible)
      - "7000:7000" # YugabyteDB master UI
      - "9000:9000" # YugabyteDB tserver UI
      # Peer nodes reach this one on the guest's pinned address at these ports.
      - "7100:7100" # master peer traffic
      - "9100:9100" # tserver peer traffic
    volumes:
      - yugabyte-data:/home/yugabyte/var
      # Overlay patched yugabyted (upstream PR #23158). See header comment.
      - /root/tack/yugabyte-overlay/yugabyted:/home/yugabyte/bin/yugabyted:ro
      # Tserver resource bounds, one flag per line with the incident notes.
      - /root/tack/yugabyte-overlay/tserver.flags:/home/yugabyte/tserver.flags:ro
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - |
          if [ -n "$$YSQL_PASSWORD" ]; then
            PGPASSWORD="$$YSQL_PASSWORD" ysqlsh -h "$$(hostname)" -p 5433 \
              -U "$$YSQL_USER" -d "$$YSQL_DB" -c 'SELECT 1' -t
          else
            /home/yugabyte/postgres/bin/pg_isready -h "$$(hostname)" -p 5433
          fi
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      # This status is informational: the deploy's rolling wait is keyed on
      # the node's tablet bootstrap progress, not on this check (TACK-488).
      # The engine has no graceful stop, so every restart replays each
      # tablet's open log segments before the SQL layer answers; the start
      # period covers a small node's replay so its status does not flap to
      # unhealthy on an ordinary restart. A full node takes longer and shows
      # unhealthy until its replay ends, then healthy again on the next
      # passing check.
      start_period: 180s

  fdb:
    # Version is set by tack's Makefile FDB_VERSION variable, also baked
    # into the Dockerfile build args and the Go bindings pin in go.mod.
    # Bump all three together via make update-fdb VERSION=...
    image: foundationdb/foundationdb:${FDB_VERSION:-7.4.6}
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      FDB_NETWORKING_MODE: container
      FDB_PORT: "4500"
      FDB_PROCESS_CLASS: unset
      # One cluster file for the server process and for every client on this
      # guest. The image defaults the server to /var/fdb/fdb.cluster, a second
      # file the clients never read, so a coordinator change the server wrote
      # there reached nobody (TACK-408).
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      # This guest's identity in the cluster, rendered by the deploy from the
      # service inventory. The address is the guest's pinned address, which
      # peers and clients on other guests reach and which survives a container
      # recreate; the zone is the guest name, which is the fault domain the
      # replication counts. Empty here so a local `docker compose up` keeps
      # announcing the container's own address and hostname.
      FDB_PUBLIC_ADDRESS: ${FDB_PUBLIC_ADDRESS:-}
      FDB_ZONE_ID: ${FDB_ZONE_ID:-}
      FDB_MACHINE_ID: ${FDB_MACHINE_ID:-}
      # The coordinator list a guest's first process starts from. The deploy
      # renders the environment's three coordinators; a guest that already has
      # a cluster file ignores this, because the cluster owns that file once it
      # exists. Empty locally, where the process is its own coordinator.
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE_CONTENTS: ${FDB_CLUSTER_FILE_CONTENTS:-}
    volumes:
      - fdb-data:/var/fdb
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      # Patched fdb.bash with IPv6 bracket handling. See fdb-overlay/fdb.bash.
      - /root/tack/fdb-overlay/fdb.bash:/var/fdb/scripts/fdb.bash:ro
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "fdbcli -C /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster --exec 'status minimal' 2>&1 | grep -q 'available'",
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # Long-lived backup_agent that streams FoundationDB continuous backups to the
  # object store. The fdbbackup session is started by `ops provision` on a host
  # whose TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS is true, and by `ops backup
  # fdb-continuous-init` for a deliberate out-of-band start; both are idempotent,
  # so an already-streaming session is left alone. This agent drains the
  # session's snapshots. The backup
  # profile keeps it off for a plain `docker compose up` without an object store,
  # and the deploy enables the profile. fdbbackup cannot resolve an IPv6 literal,
  # so it reaches the blobstore through the synthetic name fdb-blobstore-host
  # mapped to TACK_BACKUP_S3_HOST, the bare object-store address configs renders
  # alongside the full TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT.
  #
  # One agent runs per data guest. Agents divide the session's work between
  # themselves, so the count is a throughput and survival choice rather than a
  # configuration the session records: the session keeps streaming while any
  # one agent runs (TACK-408). It declares no fdb dependency, because the agent
  # retries its own connection and because a dependency would start the store
  # process on the owner guest, which runs none.
  fdb-backup-agent:
    image: foundationdb/foundationdb:${FDB_VERSION:-7.4.6}
    profiles: [backup]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 512m
    entrypoint: ["/usr/bin/backup_agent"]
    command: ["-C", "/etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster"]
    extra_hosts:
      - "fdb-blobstore-host:${TACK_BACKUP_S3_HOST}"
    volumes:
      # Writable for the same reason the app's mount is: the agent is a
      # FoundationDB client, and its client library records a coordinator
      # change in this file.
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb

  # OpenSearch, one member per search guest. Every member takes the
  # cluster_manager, data, ingest, and ml roles, and a later member joins the
  # running cluster with no Tack change. Compose starts this service only
  # when the search profile is enabled. The deploy enables the search profile
  # on the search guests and on no other guest.
  #
  # Compose interpolates node.name and the three discovery settings from the
  # TACK_SEARCH_* values in the shell environment or the rendered .env file.
  # A shell variable takes precedence over the .env file. The other values in this
  # service are literals, and the rendered override on a search guest can
  # replace them. QA sets TACK_SEARCH_DISCOVERY_TYPE to single-node.
  # Production sets TACK_SEARCH_SEED_HOSTS from the member list, and sets
  # TACK_SEARCH_INITIAL_CLUSTER_MANAGER_NODES only for the first formation of
  # tack-search1. The image entrypoint passes each non-empty dotted variable as
  # a setting, and an empty one leaves that setting unset. The rendered
  # override also configures TLS, credentials, and the address a member
  # announces to its peers.
  #
  # The search guests have no IPv4 route. java.net.preferIPv6Addresses makes
  # the JVM connect to the IPv6 address of a dual-stack host, such as the
  # model artifact host that ML Commons downloads the pinned model from.
  #
  # The ML Commons memory breaker rejects predictions when used heap is at or
  # above 85 percent. G1PeriodicGCInterval=5000 enables periodic garbage
  # collection.
  opensearch:
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch:3.8.0
    profiles: [search]
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS: -Xms3g -Xmx3g -XX:G1PeriodicGCInterval=5000 -Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true
      node.roles: cluster_manager,data,ingest,ml
      node.name: ${TACK_SEARCH_NODE_NAME:-}
      discovery.type: ${TACK_SEARCH_DISCOVERY_TYPE:-}
      discovery.seed_hosts: ${TACK_SEARCH_SEED_HOSTS:-}
      cluster.initial_cluster_manager_nodes: ${TACK_SEARCH_INITIAL_CLUSTER_MANAGER_NODES:-}
    volumes:
      - opensearch-data:/usr/share/opensearch/data
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536

  # Apache Kafka 4.x in KRaft combined broker+controller role. The audit
  # cutover uses this as the broker for the audit.events.v1 topic that the
  # producer publishes to and the audit-consumer projects into audit.events.
  #
  # The cluster ID is pinned to a value generated once on the host with:
  #
  #   docker run --rm apache/kafka:4.2.0 \
  #     /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-storage.sh random-uuid
  #
  # Persist the result into KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID in .env so a recreate does
  # not stamp a fresh metadata directory and orphan the existing logs.
  # No external port is exposed: traffic stays inside the IPv6 bridge.
  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:4.2.0
    profiles: [audit]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "1"
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:9093
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://[::]:9092,CONTROLLER://[::]:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: "1"
      KAFKA_NUM_PARTITIONS: "256"
      KAFKA_DEFAULT_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "1"
      KAFKA_MIN_INSYNC_REPLICAS: "1"
      KAFKA_UNCLEAN_LEADER_ELECTION_ENABLE: "false"
      # Empty default so the core stack parses while kafka is profile-gated off.
      # The audit-profile deploy must set KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID (a kafka-storage.sh
      # random-uuid) in .env before enabling the audit profile.
      CLUSTER_ID: ${KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID:-}
    volumes:
      - kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD-SHELL
        - /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 >/dev/null 2>&1
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # ClickHouse single-node OLAP store for the Wave 1 audit consumer.
  # Internal-only: 8123 (HTTP) and 9000 (native) are not exposed to the
  # host. Apache 2.0 image so the open-source-only constraint holds.
  clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.5
    profiles: [audit]
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 2g
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DEFAULT_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: "1"
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O - http://[::1]:8123/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

  # Wave 1 audit-consumer. Uses the same image as the app container; the
  # entrypoint is overridden to /usr/local/bin/audit-consumer so the
  # binary built by the Dockerfile is invoked directly. Mounts the
  # signing key for the embedded notarizer.
  audit-consumer:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-audit-consumer:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [audit]
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.audit-consumer
      args:
        COMMIT: ${TACK_COMMIT:-unknown}
        BUILD_TIME: ${TACK_BUILD_TIME:-unknown}
        TAG: ${TACK_TAG:-dev}
        DIRTY: ${TACK_DIRTY:-false}
    restart: unless-stopped
    mem_limit: 1g
    entrypoint: ["/usr/local/bin/audit-consumer"]
    environment:
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_BROKERS: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_BROKERS:-kafka:9092}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_TOPIC: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_KAFKA_TOPIC:-audit.events.v1}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID:-tack-audit-projector}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_BATCH_SIZE: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_BATCH_SIZE:-256}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_POLL_INTERVAL: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_POLL_INTERVAL:-250ms}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_YUGABYTE_DSN: ${AUDIT_WRITER_DSN}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_CLICKHOUSE_DSN: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_CLICKHOUSE_DSN:-clickhouse://default:@clickhouse:9000/audit}
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_KEY_PATH:-/etc/tack/audit-signing.pem}
      # The guest whose key signs, stamped on every notarization as its
      # claimed origin (TACK-437). The configs deploy renders the guest's
      # inventory name; empty falls back to the container's hostname.
      AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_HOST: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_SIGNING_HOST:-}
      # Set this to enable the FoundationDB half of the operator relay. It is
      # deliberately not hardcoded: a set-but-unreadable cluster file makes the
      # consumer refuse to start, which would also stop the YugabyteDB relay
      # and halt every operator event, not just the FoundationDB ones. Leaving
      # it unset on a host without that mount runs the YugabyteDB half alone.
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: ${AUDIT_CONSUMER_FDB_CLUSTER_FILE:-}
      # The same ENV the app requires, read the same way, so every consumer
      # log line names its environment (TACK-263).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-debug}
      LOG_JSON_FILE: /var/log/tack/audit-consumer.jsonl
      LOG_TEXT_FILE: /var/log/tack/audit-consumer.log
      LOG_MAX_BACKUPS: ${LOG_MAX_BACKUPS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS: ${LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-0}
      LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB: ${LOG_MAX_SIZE_MB:-100}
    volumes:
      - tack-logs:/var/log/tack
      - /etc/tack:/etc/tack:ro
      # Writable: this process is a FoundationDB client too, and the client
      # library records a coordinator change in this file (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
    # No yugabyte dependency: deployed guests reach the ledger on the data
    # guests through the rendered env's multi-host DSN; the startup ping
    # retries until the ledger answers, so ordering is not load-bearing.
    depends_on:
      kafka:
        condition: service_started
      clickhouse:
        condition: service_healthy

  # Short-lived operator-invoked container for backup, verify, and
  # restore-test operations. The profiles: [ops] tag keeps it out of the
  # default docker compose up; invoke via:
  #   docker compose run --rm tack-ops ops backup [subcommand] [args]
  tack-ops:
    image: ghcr.io/agoodkind/tack-server:${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [ops]
    mem_limit: 512m
    entrypoint: ["/server"]
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      # tack-ops uses network_mode: host so all services are reachable by
      # loopback. DATABASE_URL must be set in the host .env as a full DSN
      # pointing at 127.0.0.1:5433; the app service's DSN targets yugabyte
      # and cannot be reused here.
      DATABASE_URL: ${TACK_OPS_DATABASE_URL}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_OPERATOR_DSN:-}
      # Ledger read and redaction for the `audit query`, `audit get`,
      # `audit export`, and `audit redact-actor` host commands. Loopback DSNs
      # like the operator one above; empty until the host .env renders them.
      AUDIT_READER_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_READER_DSN:-}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN: ${TACK_OPS_AUDIT_REDACTOR_DSN:-}
      # The valid signer set (TACK-437), the same value the app carries, so
      # `audit verify` here judges a bundle's signer. `audit signers` still
      # runs through the app service: this container mounts no signing key.
      AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS: ${AUDIT_VALID_SIGNERS:-}
      FDB_CLUSTER_FILE: /etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster
      FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT: ${FDB_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT:-5s}
      # The redundancy mode `ops provision` configures on a store that has
      # never been configured. single is the local and single-guest value;
      # an environment running one process per data guest renders double, so
      # a rebuilt environment comes back with the replication it had rather
      # than with one copy of every key (TACK-408).
      TACK_OPS_FDB_REDUNDANCY_MODE: ${TACK_OPS_FDB_REDUNDANCY_MODE:-single}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      # Same ENV the app requires, read the same way. A default here would
      # make one variable name mean two things in one stack file, so a host
      # whose .env said development would still run this container as
      # production (TACK-261).
      ENV: ${ENV:?ENV is required, set it in .env}
      # The dumps connect as
      # tack_migrator with TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD below.
      YUGABYTE_DB: ${YUGABYTE_DB:?YUGABYTE_DB is required, set it in .env}
      # Audit role passwords for `ops audit seed-roles`, which creates or rotates
      # the LOGIN audit roles. Empty default so other ops (backup) run without
      # them; the seed-roles command errors loudly when they are unset.
      AUDIT_WRITER_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_WRITER_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_READER_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_READER_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_REDACTOR_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_REDACTOR_PASSWORD:-}
      AUDIT_OPERATOR_PASSWORD: ${AUDIT_OPERATOR_PASSWORD:-}
      # The application login's password, set by the same seed-roles run
      # (TACK-180); the app service reads it inside its DATABASE_URL.
      TACK_APP_PASSWORD: ${TACK_APP_PASSWORD:-}
      TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD: ${TACK_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD:-}
      # Object store for engine-native continuous backup. Read by the FDB
      # continuous backup path to build the blobstore destination URL.
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_REGION:-us-east-1}
      TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN: ${TACK_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET_MAIN:-tack-backups}
      # Master quorum for the backup one-shot containers. The deploy renders
      # the value from the ledger topology; the fallback is the dev single
      # node, matching the compiled default.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_MASTER_ADDRESSES: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_MASTER_ADDRESSES:-yugabyte:7100}
      # Ledger node names paired with their guests' addresses (TACK-460), so
      # the SQL dumpers can dial an encrypted node by the name its
      # certificate carries. The deploy renders it; empty in the clear.
      TACK_LEDGER_NODE_HOSTS: ${TACK_LEDGER_NODE_HOSTS:-}
      # The ledger's own image, from the anchor the yugabyte service uses. The
      # backup tooling (yb-admin, ysql_dump, ysql_dumpall) and the restore
      # drill's throwaway engine run it, so a rehearsal restores into the
      # version the cluster runs and the dumper matches the server. There is
      # no compiled default: a default in the binary drifted to 2025.2 against
      # this 2024.2 cluster, and the drill's schema apply failed on it.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_IMAGE: *yugabyte_image
      # Snapshot-export paths. Deliberately no fallback: the commands that
      # need them error loudly when unset, per the config contract, rather
      # than tar or restore against a wrong location.
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_ROCKSDB_DIR: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_ROCKSDB_DIR:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_YB_OVERLAY_PATH: ${TACK_BACKUP_YB_OVERLAY_PATH:-}
      # Backup staleness alarm mail. A staleness-check run that first finds a
      # mechanism past its threshold mails a plain-words account of the fault.
      # Empty recipient mails nothing, which is the local default; the deploy
      # renders the address.
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_EMAIL: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_EMAIL:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_MSMTPRC: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_MSMTPRC:-/etc/msmtprc}
      # Deputy staleness alarm (TACK-481): the primary checker's service name,
      # the window its run must appear in, and the in-run grace before the
      # deputy takes over. An empty service means this checker is the primary.
      # Without this pass-through a data guest's check ran as a primary and
      # mailed a second time for the same fault.
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_SERVICE: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_SERVICE:-}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_WINDOW_SECONDS: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_WINDOW_SECONDS:-1500}
      TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_GRACE_SECONDS: ${TACK_BACKUP_ALARM_PRIMARY_GRACE_SECONDS:-90}
      # FoundationDB continuous backup. Without this pass-through the container
      # falls back to the compiled default false, so `ops provision` leaves the
      # stream off and the restore drill and staleness check skip their FDB legs
      # on a host whose .env says true. The overlay path is the patched fdb.bash
      # the deploy places on the guest, which the restore drill bind-mounts into
      # its throwaway cluster; deliberately no fallback, so the drill errors
      # loudly when it is unset rather than mounting a wrong file.
      TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS: ${TACK_BACKUP_FDB_CONTINUOUS:-false}
      TACK_BACKUP_FDB_OVERLAY_PATH: ${TACK_BACKUP_FDB_OVERLAY_PATH:-}
      # Ledger transport encryption (TACK-460). The ledger DSNs above already
      # carry sslmode and the authority's path; these two are for the engine's
      # administration tool, which the backup and snapshot commands run in
      # one-shot containers and which takes its certificate directory as a
      # flag. Without the pass-through those commands dial an encrypted
      # cluster with no certificates and fail to connect.
      TACK_LEDGER_TLS_ENABLED: ${TACK_LEDGER_TLS_ENABLED:-false}
      TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR: ${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-}
      # The tag this stack pins the app images at, so `ops deploy verify`
      # checks the running containers against the image the deploy named.
      TACK_IMAGE_TAG: ${TACK_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    volumes:
      - /root/backups:/root/backups
      # Writable: the ops commands that open the product store are
      # FoundationDB clients, and the client library records a coordinator
      # change in this file (TACK-408).
      - /etc/foundationdb:/etc/foundationdb
      # The staleness alarm reads the guest's SMTP account out of this file and
      # then speaks SMTP itself, so the file is all it needs: no msmtp binary
      # lives in this image, and nothing here execs one.
      - /etc/msmtprc:/etc/msmtprc:ro
      # The ledger's certificate authority, for the DSNs above and for the
      # one-shots this container starts. Only the certificate directory, not
      # the whole of /etc/tack: the audit signing key lives beside it and this
      # container deliberately holds no signing key.
      - ${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-/etc/tack/ledger-certs}:${TACK_LEDGER_CERTS_DIR:-/etc/tack/ledger-certs}:ro
      # Docker socket mount is intentional for this short-lived ops container:
      # the backup binary orchestrates scratch containers on the local daemon.
      # This exception is explicitly scoped to tack-ops and must not be added
      # to the long-running app service. See the sibling-container architecture
      # decision in CLAUDE.md under the Deployment section.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

volumes:
  yugabyte-data:
  fdb-data:
  tack-logs:
  kafka-data:
  clickhouse-data:
  opensearch-data:

# IPv6-only bridge. The per-host /96 is carved from the host's on-link /64 and
# NDP-proxied back onto eth0 by ndppd, so containers source out as real GUAs
# (gateway_mode_v6 is routed, no masquerade). Inter-container DNS returns AAAA
# only because enable_ipv4 is false. Do not flip back to dual-stack: that defeats
# the forced-v6 contract. The subnet and gateway are per host and come from the
# configs render (tack_docker_v6_subnet / tack_docker_v6_gateway); the defaults
# are the production prefix so an unrendered env still parses.
networks:
  default:
    enable_ipv6: true
    enable_ipv4: false
    driver_opts:
      com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_v6: routed
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${TACK_DOCKER_V6_SUBNET:-3d06:bad:b01:0:7ac::/96}
          gateway: ${TACK_DOCKER_V6_GATEWAY:-3d06:bad:b01:0:7ac::1}
